passage.text: Dao Srisuk grew up in a small village in northeastern Thailand, where her parents grow rice.
passage.reading: ˈdaʊ ˈsriːsʊk ˈɡruː ˈʌp ɪn ə ˈsmɔːl ˈvɪlɪdʒ ɪn ˌnɔːrθˈiːstərn ˈtaɪlænd, wɛr hɜːr ˈpɛrənts ˈɡroʊ ˈraɪs.

passage.text: When she was twelve, a teacher saw how fast she could run and asked her to join the school team.
passage.reading: wɛn ʃiː wʌz ˈtwɛlv, ə ˈtiːtʃər ˈsɔː ˈhaʊ ˈfæst ʃiː kʊd ˈrʌn ənd ˈæskt hɜːr tə ˈdʒɔɪn ðə ˈskuːl ˈtiːm.

passage.text: At first, Dao only ran for fun.
passage.reading: ət ˈfɜːrst, ˈdaʊ ˈoʊnli ˈræn fər ˈfʌn.

passage.text: At fifteen, she moved to Bangkok to practice at a sports school.
passage.reading: ət ˌfɪfˈtiːn, ʃiː ˈmuːvd tə ˈbæŋkɑːk tə ˈpræktɪs ət ə ˈspɔːrts ˈskuːl.

passage.text: It was a big sacrifice for her and her family.
passage.reading: ɪt wʌz ə ˈbɪɡ ˈsækrəfaɪs fər hɜːr ənd hɜːr ˈfæməli.

passage.text: She could only go home twice a year, and she often felt lonely.
passage.reading: ʃiː kʊd ˈoʊnli ˈɡoʊ ˈhoʊm ˈtwaɪs ə ˈjɪr, ənd ʃiː ˈɔːfən ˈfɛlt ˈloʊnli.

passage.text: Every day, she got up at five and ran for three hours before school.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈdeɪ, ʃiː ˈɡɑːt ˈʌp ət ˈfaɪv ənd ˈræn fər ˈθriː ˈaʊərz bɪˈfɔːr ˈskuːl.

passage.text: When she was nineteen, she had a serious knee injury.
passage.reading: wɛn ʃiː wʌz ˌnaɪnˈtiːn, ʃiː ˈhæd ə ˈsɪriəs ˈniː ˈɪndʒəri.

passage.text: Doctors told her that she might never run again.
passage.reading: ˈdɑːktərz ˈtoʊld hɜːr ðæt ʃiː maɪt ˈnɛvər ˈrʌn əˈɡɛn.

passage.text: It was the biggest difficulty of her life, and she almost gave up.
passage.reading: ɪt wʌz ðə ˈbɪɡɪst ˈdɪfɪkəlti əv hɜːr ˈlaɪf, ənd ʃiː ˈɔːlmoʊst ˈɡeɪv ˈʌp.

passage.text: But after a year of hard work, she was running again.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈæftər ə ˈjɪr əv ˈhɑːrd ˈwɜːrk, ʃiː wʌz ˈrʌnɪŋ əˈɡɛn.

passage.text: At twenty-four, Dao finally ran at the Olympic Games.
passage.reading: ət ˈtwɛnti ˈfɔːr, ˈdaʊ ˈfaɪnəli ˈræn ət ði oʊˈlɪmpɪk ˈɡeɪmz.

passage.text: She didn't win a medal, but she set a new Thai record, and everyone in her village watched her on TV.
passage.reading: ʃiː ˈdɪdənt ˈwɪn ə ˈmɛdəl, bʌt ʃiː ˈsɛt ə ˈnuː ˈtaɪ ˈrɛkərd, ənd ˈɛvriwʌn ɪn hɜːr ˈvɪlɪdʒ ˈwɑːtʃt hɜːr ɑːn ˌtiːˈviː.

passage.text: "Being an athlete isn't only about winning," she says.
passage.reading: ˈbiːɪŋ ən ˈæθliːt ˈɪzənt ˈoʊnli əˈbaʊt ˈwɪnɪŋ, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "It's about getting up again every time you fall."
passage.reading: ɪts əˈbaʊt ˈɡɛtɪŋ ˈʌp əˈɡɛn ˈɛvri ˈtaɪm juː ˈfɔːl.
